evidence: Single package ('websocket_server') with clear module separation (thread.py, websocket_server.py, __init__.py)
Repository tree shows flat directory structure with max depth 2, typical of a monolith
Server logic centralized in WebsocketServer class inheriting from ThreadingMixIn and TCPServer, with internal handler (WebSocketHandler) for protocol logic
Test suite organized in tests/ directory but tightly coupled to internal implementation (imports internal classes like WebSocketHandler, WebsocketServerThread)
API surface exposed via WebsocketServer class methods (run_forever, send_message, etc.) used directly by server.py and tests
No external service boundaries, inter-process communication, or deployment isolation — all components run in same process
Low fan-out (avg 3.5) and few packages (1) indicate cohesive, internally modular design rather than distributed or service-oriented
risks: Tight coupling between core server logic and threading/handling components may hinder testability and modifiability
Monolithic structure may scale poorly under high concurrency without architectural refactoring
Lack of clear separation between infrastructure (networking) and domain logic could reduce long-term maintainability
